I am currently in a 12 week anxiety management program that is run jointly by my college and an association for anxiety disorders in my province.

One thing we focus on when we 'check-in' and 'check-out' are simple relaxation techniques.

These techniques are usually deep breathing exercises and stretching exercises. They are also pretty subtle in movement so you can do them anywhere when your anxiety is high.

So far my favourite stretch includes the shoulders. This is because when you get high anxiety, your body will show physical signs of that and one of the signs is feeling tense somewhere. For me, it's the lower neck area and into the shoulders.

The stretch is simple. You lift your shoulders as high as you can to your ears, hold it for a count of three to five, and then completely relax them.

You can pair that with breathing in deep and slow as you raise your shoulders, holding your breath for the count, and exhaling when you relax your shoulders.

It's really useful for just taking a mental step back and recognizing how your shoulders or other areas may feel when you get anxious. You can also repeat this multiple times until you've calmed down the anxiety a bit, like in a test or even just in class.

Do you guys know of other techniques like these? Do you have a favourite?

I can also share more if you would like.
